feedback: If the child picks an operation from a single word, ask them to lay out known vs unknown first and justify the step order from the relationships.
Praise plans that name what is unknown and defer computing until the structure is clear.
activities.intendedInsight: The plan should come from the structure of the problem, not from matching keywords to operations, which is unreliable and breaks down on multi-step problems.
learnerActions: Before touching the numbers, write down what is known and what is unknown in the problem.
Represent the unknown explicitly — with a letter or a bar — rather than rushing to combine numbers.
State a plan for the order of steps, explaining why that order, based on how the quantities relate rather than on cue words.
Discuss why a cue word (e.g. 'altogether', 'left') can point to the wrong operation on a multi-step problem.
activities.title: Known/unknown analysis before computing

feedback: Use these items alongside richer problem-solving work, not as a substitute: a scored linear format can check estimation and magnitude judgements but does not itself elicit the independent planning or monitoring a long solution requires.
If a child rejects 250% of a jug as nonsense, probe: a jug is a unit you can need more than one of, so 250% means 2.5 jugs — distinguish 'part of a fixed group' from 'multiples of a reference unit'.
activities.intendedInsight: Estimation brackets a calculation and magnitude sense tells whether a percentage or decimal result is possible in context — and over-100% is not automatically impossible (2.5 jugs is fine) when the whole is a reference unit you can need more than one of, rather than a fixed group.
learnerActions: Answer short targeted questions such as 'Which computed answer must be wrong by estimation?' and 'Can 130% of the class pass?'
For a counterexample like 'A jug holds 2 litres; a recipe needs 250% of the jug — what does that mean?', decide whether it is nonsense or a sensible 2.5 jugs, and explain your reasoning.
Explain in each case how rounding or the 100%-is-the-whole idea drove your judgement.
activities.title: Estimation and magnitude-sense targeted items
